This provision (§1.01) is a Definitions section; it contains no independently operative permission/prohibition/ratio-test rule of its own, so no WireRule entries were produced - only WireDefinition entries for the five defined terms materially present in the supplied text ('Applicable Liquidity Threshold', 'Applicable Rate', 'Appropriate Lender', 'Approved Fund', 'Asset Sale'), plus 'RCF Increase Amount' which is defined inline within the Applicable Liquidity Threshold definition.

'Applicable Rate' is split into two WireDefinition entries (Term Benchmark Loans track and Base Rate Loans track) sharing the same termName, because the IR has no native way to bind two parallel per-category outputs to a single definition node (see irExtensionCandidates).

The quantitative values detected in the cross-referenced regions (Section 10.07, 6.01, 6.02(1), 8.01(1)) - e.g. $1.0 million minimum assignment amount, $3,500 processing fee, 90/45/5/10 day periods, specific 2022/2023 dates - belong to OTHER sections' own economics (assignment mechanics, financial-statement delivery deadlines, non-payment cure periods) and are not part of the Applicable Liquidity Threshold / Applicable Rate / Asset Sale definitions being compiled here; they were not consumed because they do not carry any value within this provision's own operative text.

Cross-references to Sections 7.01, 7.02, 7.03(excl. (6)/(7)), 7.05, and Internal Revenue Code Section 1031 within the Asset Sale definition were preserved via citations on the relevant TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE nodes rather than resolved, since Asset Sale's own definitional test does not require knowing those sections' full substantive content (it simply asks whether a transaction is 'permitted' under them, an external boolean fact).

Two AMBIGUOUS_TARGET-flagged definitions appearing in Phase 2 context ('Benchmark', 'Floor', 'Benchmark Replacement', 'NYFRB Rate') were not relied upon anywhere in this compilation's economics, so their ambiguity does not affect any rule/definition submitted here.

SECTION 10.07 Successors and Assigns.

(a) The provisions of this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and
registered assigns permitted hereby, except that the Borrower may not, except as permitted by Section 7.03 and the last sentence of this clause (a), assign or otherwise transfer any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior
written consent of the Administrative Agent and each Lender and no Lender may assign or otherwise transfer any of its rights or obligations hereunder (including to existing Lenders and their Affiliates) except (i) to an assignee in accordance
with the provisions of Section 10.07(b) (such an assignee, an “Eligible Assignee”), (ii) by way of participation in accordance with the provisions of Section 10.07(d), or (iii) by way of pledge or assignment of a
security interest subject to the restrictions of Section 10.07(f), or (iv) to an SPC in accordance with the provisions of Section 10.07(g) (and any other attempted assignment or transfer by any party hereto shall be null and void)..
Nothing in this Agreement, expressed or implied, shall be construed to confer upon any Person (other than the parties hereto, their respective successors and assigns permitted hereby, Participants to the extent provided in Section 10.07(d) and,
to the extent expressly contemplated hereby, Related Persons of each of the Administrative Agent, the Collateral Agent and the Lenders) any legal or equitable right, remedy or claim under or by reason of this Agreement.

(b) Assignments by Lenders. Any Lender may at any time assign to one or more assignees all or a portion of its rights and obligations
under this Agreement (including all or a portion of its Commitment and the Loans at the time owing to it); provided that any such assignment shall be subject to the following conditions:

findings.verifierReasoning: The source makes the Pricing Level 1 override during a late-Compliance-Certificate or continuing-Event-of-Default period conditional on an affirmative election 'at the option of the Required Facility Lenders' -- it is not automatic. The proposed IR's attempted expression tree treats the occurrence of either triggering fact (late CC or continuing EOD) as itself sufficient to force Pricing Level 1, with no boolean gate representing the Required Facility Lenders' election. Under the real contract, absent that election the ratio-based (or delivery-based) pricing continues to apply even while a CC is late or an EOD is continuing. A downstream consumer relying on this attempted structure (even though currently marked UNSUPPORTED/AMBIGUOUS) would, once repaired, compute an automatically higher rate in a scenario where the real agreement in fact permits the lower ratio-based rate to continue absent lender election -- this changes the applicable interest rate conclusion and is a real, independently operative condition dropped from the representation.
